subject: maths
question:
If the mode of the given data is 22.75, find the median. (Round off to two decimal places)

 
 

 Class Interval
 0-7
 7-14
 14-21
 21-28
 28-35
 35-42
 
 

 Frequency
 1
 7
 9
 11
 X
 3
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

From Mode = 22.75, the modal class is 21-28. Here l = 21, h = 7, f₁ = 11, f₀ = 9, f₂ = X.

Mode = 21 + [2 / (22 − 9 − X)] × 7 ⇒ 1.75 = 14 / (13 − X) ⇒ X = 5.

Total frequency N = 36 ⇒ N/2 = 18.

Cumulative frequency before the median class (21-28) is 17.

Median = 21 + [(18 − 17) / 11] × 7 = 21 + 0.636 ≈ 21.64.

**∴ The correct answer is 21.64.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Mode = 22.75 (Modal class is 21-28)

Lower limit (l) = 21, Class size (h) = 7

Frequency of modal class (f₁) = 11

Frequency of preceding class (f₀) = 9

Frequency of succeeding class (f₂) = X

**Formula Used:**

Mode = l + [ (f₁ − f₀) / (2f₁ − f₀ − f₂) ] × h

Median = l + [ (N/2 − cf) / f ] × h

**Calculation:**

⇒ 22.75 = 21 + [ (11 − 9) / (2 × 11 − 9 − X) ] × 7

⇒ 1.75 = [ 2 / (13 − X) ] × 7

⇒ 13 − X = 14 / 1.75

⇒ 13 − X = 8 ⇒ X = 5

Cumulative frequencies (cf) for the classes:

⇒ 0-7: 1

⇒ 7-14: 1 + 7 = 8

⇒ 14-21: 8 + 9 = 17

⇒ 21-28: 17 + 11 = 28

⇒ 28-35: 28 + 5 = 33

⇒ 35-42: 33 + 3 = 36

⇒ Total frequency N = 36 ⇒ N / 2 = 18

The cumulative frequency just greater than 18 is 28, so the median class is 21-28.

⇒ l = 21, h = 7, cf = 17, f = 11

⇒ Median = 21 + [ (18 − 17) / 11 ] × 7

⇒ Median = 21 + 7 / 11

⇒ Median = 21 + 0.6363... ≈ 21.64

**∴ The correct answer is 21.64.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Empirical Relationship

For a moderately skewed distribution, the relationship between mean, median, and mode is given by: Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean.

Mode of Grouped Data

Mode = l + [ (f₁ − f₀) / (2f₁ − f₀ − f₂) ] × h, where f₁ is the frequency of the modal class, f₀ is of the preceding class, and f₂ is of the succeeding class.

Median of Grouped Data

Median = l + [ (N/2 − cf) / f ] × h, where cf is the cumulative frequency of the class preceding the median class, and f is the frequency of the median class.
